svg.title: The Customs Broker Operating Model
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-customs-broker-operating-model; chapter number: 11; title: The Customs Broker Operating Model; subtitle: A licensed agent whose authority comes from a direct POA; caption: A broker's authority comes entirely from a properly executed direct power of attorney. The license survives only through demonstrable responsible supervision and control.; assumptions note: CBP sets no staffing ratio and judges each operation case by case, so no headcount is assigned. Fee and exam figures are as the practitioners reported them.; note: Sources are CH Powell Company, Braumiller Law Group, PLLC, CONECT Recorded Webinars, Ask The Customs Manager, Steve Fodor, Nadeem Virk and Factory Floor Economics.; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Licensed Customs Broker; headcount: No staffing ratio; CBP judges each operation case by case; focus: Responsible supervision and control under direct POAs; $150-250 per standard entry and $250-400 for complex work; spokes: role: Importer of Record; type: Principal under a direct POA; kpi: Confirms the broker actually remits duties, because the IOR stays liable if the broker fails to pay; role: Surety; type: Continuous bond provider; kpi: Around $400-500 a year when the bond is bought direct rather than through the broker; role: CBP Broker Management; type: Regulator under modernized Part 111; kpi: 72-hour breach reporting; individual license fee raised from $200 to $300; role: CBLE Candidate; type: Licensing pipeline; kpi: 60 of 80 correct in 4.5 hours, open book; classification is the largest section with 15-20 questions
